title: Extended Čech model for derived closed support
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $r\geq0$, and let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Put $Z=V(I)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(A):I\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $D(A)$ for the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A)$ for its full subcategory of objects whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion, meaning every element is killed by some power of $I$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. The inclusion $D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A)\to D(A)$ has a right adjoint $R\Gamma_Z$. For $g\in A$, let $A_g$ be localization at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Define the cochain complex $C_A^\bullet(f)$ by $C_A^0=A$, by $C_A^q=\prod_{1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_q\leq r}A_{f_{i_1}\cdots f_{i_q}}$ for $1\leq q\leq r$, and by zero in other degrees. Its degree-zero differential is diagonal localization; for $q\geq1$, its component into the factor indexed by $i_1<\cdots<i_{q+1}$ is the sum of the localization maps from the factors with $i_a$ deleted, with coefficient $(-1)^{a-1}$. Then, for every $A$-module $M$ viewed in degree zero and every $j\geq0$, there is a natural $A$-linear isomorphism $H^j(C_A^\bullet(f)\otimes_A M)\cong H^j(R\Gamma_Z(M))$. The tensor here is ordinary termwise tensor, with differential $d\otimes1_M$. For $r=0$, the complex is $A$ in degree zero and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

source.place: Tag 0A6R (lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint), the explicit extended Čech right-adjoint model and its module specialization.

proof.text: Write $C=C_A^\bullet(f)$. The displayed differential squares to zero: deleting two different indices in the two possible orders gives the same localization map with opposite signs. For any integer-indexed complex $K$, set $F(K)=\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_A K)$, with $F(K)^n=\bigoplus_{q=0}^r C^q\otimes_A K^{n-q}$ and total differential $d_C\otimes1+(-1)^q1\otimes d_K$ on horizontal degree $q$. The finite products in $C^q$ are finite direct sums. For a nonempty subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $g_S=\prod_{i\in S}f_i$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with base $A$, module $A$ and the powers of $g_S$ identifies $A_{g_S}\otimes_A K^m$ with $(K^m)_{g_S}$, naturally in $K^m$; the map sends $(a/g_S^t)\otimes x$ to $ax/g_S^t$. For the empty subset the identification is $A\otimes_A K^m=K^m$. Identity on horizontal degree zero and zero on positive horizontal degrees defines a natural cochain map $\epsilon_K:F(K)\to K$: projecting the total differential to horizontal degree zero leaves exactly $d_K$.

source.place: Tag 0A6R (lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint), construction of the total complex and its map to K; explicit signs as in more-algebra.tex, section-extended-alternating-cech-complex.

proof.text: Each $A_{g_S}$ is flat over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. The degree-zero term $A$ is flat because $A\otimes_A-$ is the identity. Finite direct sums of flat modules are flat: tensoring a finite sum is the sum of the tensor functors, and the kernel and image of a finite direct sum of module maps are the sums of their kernels and images. Thus every term of $C$ is flat, and $C^q=0$ for $q>r$. Apply [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] to $C$. By the equivalent quasi-isomorphism criterion in [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], $K\mapsto F(K)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, without a boundedness assumption on $K$. Consequently the localization defining $D(A)$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives an endofunctor, still denoted $F$, and the natural transformation $\epsilon:F\to\mathrm{id}$ descends with it.

source.place: Tag 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism), applied to the bounded flat complex in dualizing.tex Tag 0A6R; algebra.tex Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization).

proof.text: Suppose $r>0$ and fix $a\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$. Localize the total complex at $f_a$. For a subset $S$ not containing $a$, the localization map from the $S$-column to the $(S\cup\{a\})$-column is now invertible: $f_a$ already acts invertibly, and its inverse on fractions is multiplication by the corresponding negative power, using [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. On this localized total define a degree $-1$ map by $(hx)_S=0$ if $a\in S$, and $(hx)_S=(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s<a\}|}x_{S\cup\{a\}}$ otherwise, using the inverse localization map to interpret the latter entry in the $S$-column and keeping the vertical degree fixed. In $d_Ch+hd_C$, the term inserting/deleting $a$ is $x_S$; each term involving another index occurs twice, with signs differing by one transposition, and cancels. Hence $d_Ch+hd_C=1$. The vertical terms cancel because $h$ changes the horizontal degree by $-1$, so their coefficients are $(-1)^{q-1}$ and $(-1)^q$. Therefore $Dh+hD=1$ for the total differential $D$, proving $(F(K))_{f_a}$ contractible. This computation also covers the empty subset and the top horizontal degree.

source.place: Tag 0G6J (lemma-extended-alternating-homotopy-zero), insertion homotopy, written with the positive-identity sign for the differential in this item and extended to the total with arbitrary K.

proof.text: Localization is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^n(F(K))_{f_a}\cong H^n((F(K))_{f_a})=0$ for every $n$ and $a$. Fix $x\in H^n(F(K))$. The zero-fraction criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives integers $n_a\geq1$ with $f_a^{n_a}x=0$. Let $N=\max_a n_a$. Every generating monomial of $I^{r(N-1)+1}$ contains some $f_a^N$, so every such monomial kills $x$; its $A$-linear combinations kill $x$ as well. Thus $I^{r(N-1)+1}x=0$. By [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], all cohomology modules of $F(K)$ are $I$-power torsion. If $r=0$, then $I=(0)$ and $I^1$ kills every element, so the same conclusion holds directly. Thus $F$ takes values in the required full subcategory.

source.place: Tag 0G6K (lemma-extended-alternating-torsion), localization argument; applied to total complexes using the explicit homotopy in Step 3.

proof.text: Let $L\in D(A)$ have $I$-power torsion cohomology, and let $S$ be a nonempty subset of the generators. If $I^t x=0$, then $g_S^t x=0$, because $g_S\in I$. The fraction criterion and exactness of localization therefore give $H^n(L_{g_S})=H^n(L)_{g_S}=0$, using [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. In particular $L_{g_S}=0$ in $D(A_{g_S})$. Localization $V\mapsto V_{g_S}$ is left adjoint to restriction $U$ from $A_{g_S}$-modules: the inverse to restriction of a map is $v/g_S^t\mapsto g_S^{-t}\phi(v)$, which is well defined by the fraction equality criterion and is the unique extension. Restriction is exact, since its kernels and images are the same underlying modules; localization is exact by the cited lemma. The exact-derived adjunction of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] consequently gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(L,U(N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_{g_S})}(L_{g_S},N)=0$ for every $N\in D(A_{g_S})$. This applies to every shift of the localized complex $K_{g_S}$.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), for exact localization and restriction; this spells out the Hom-vanishing needed in the final paragraph of dualizing.tex Tag 0A6R.

proof.text: Let $T_{\geq q}(K)$ be the subcomplex of $F(K)$ formed from horizontal columns of degree at least $q$, for $1\leq q\leq r+1$. It is a subcomplex since the horizontal differential raises $q$ and the vertical differential preserves it. We have $T_{\geq r+1}(K)=0$. The quotient $B_q=T_{\geq q}(K)/T_{\geq q+1}(K)$ is the finite direct sum of the complexes $U(K_{g_S})[-q]$ with $|S|=q$: its differential is $(-1)^q d_K$, exactly the differential of that shift. The degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to T_{\geq q+1}(K)\to T_{\geq q}(K)\to B_q\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. For every integer $m$, Step 5 gives $\operatorname{Hom}(L,B_q[m])=0$, since a map to a finite direct sum is determined by its components. Descend from $q=r+1$ to $q=1$: exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(L,T_{\geq q+1}(K)[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(L,T_{\geq q}(K)[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(L,B_q[m])$ from [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] makes the middle group zero whenever the first is zero. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(L,T_{\geq1}(K)[m])=0$ for all $m$. This is a finite induction even for unbounded $K$.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor) and Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), finite column filtration spelling out the adjunction assertion at the end of dualizing.tex Tag 0A6R.

proof.text: Projection to horizontal degree zero gives a degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to T_{\geq1}(K)\to F(K)\xrightarrow{\epsilon_K}K\to0$. Its distinguished triangle is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The vanishing from Step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], applied also to the rotated triangle, show that composition with $\epsilon_K$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(L,F(K))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(L,K)$: its kernel is the image of the zero group $\operatorname{Hom}(L,T_{\geq1}(K))$, and every map $L\to K$ lifts because its composite to $T_{\geq1}(K)[1]$ is zero. These bijections are natural in $L$ and $K$, since they are composition with the natural map $\epsilon_K$; their inverses are natural by uniqueness of lifts. Step 4 places $F(K)$ in the torsion subcategory, whose Hom sets are the same as those of $D(A)$ by fullness. Therefore these are precisely the adjunction bijections for the inclusion as left adjoint and $F$ as right adjoint. Set $R\Gamma_Z=F$.

source.place: Tag 0A6R (lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint), final paragraph, with the explicit orthogonality and finite-filtration argument of Steps 5–6.

proof.text: For $K=M[0]$, the total complex defining $F(K)$ has exactly one summand in each total degree, namely $C^q\otimes_A M$ in degree $q$. Its differential is $d_C\otimes1_M$, because the differential of $M[0]$ is zero. Hence it is literally the ordinary termwise tensor complex in the statement. Taking the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] yields the required natural $A$-linear isomorphisms $H^j(C\otimes_A M)\cong H^j(R\Gamma_Z(M))$ for every $j\geq0$. If $r=0$, the total functor and its projection are the identity, and every cohomology module is $(0)$-power torsion as checked in Step 4; thus the inclusion and its right adjoint are the identity and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, including the zero ring. This also supplies the adjunction directly in that case.

source.place: Tag 0A6R (lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint), module specialization and empty generating list.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A6R (lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint), same explicit total functor and counit. The image-torsion verification uses the written insertion contraction of more-algebra.tex Tags 0G6J/0G6K in place of the Koszul-colimit check, and the final adjunction is expanded by exact-localization orthogonality and a finite column filtration.

split_report.summary: Proved the extended localization total functor is the right adjoint using its K-flatness, an explicit localized insertion contraction, and a finite-filtration Hom-vanishing argument from the exact localization/restriction adjunction. Specialized to modules, including r=0. Statement unchanged; all inputs reuse existing DAG nodes; no new nodes or Lean work.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q135-2534daa99 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement agrees with Stacks 0A6R (dualizing.tex l.1248-1320), hypothesis by hypothesis: any commutative ring, I=(f_1..f_r), r=0 allowed, specialized to modules, where ⊗^L is the termwise tensor because C is bounded and termwise flat. Nothing is weakened. No new nodes; review_split.py gives PASS. Steps 1-2: the localization-tensor identification, flatness of A_g plus finite sums, and the generic K-flatness lemma, so F descends to D(A) with no boundedness on K. I accept the declared tool use of lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat as generic K-flatness. Step 3: I recomputed the insertion contraction with sign (-1)^{#{s<a}}. It gives dh+hd=+1, against 0G6J's -1 with its (-1)^j; the vertical terms cancel, and the empty and top columns are covered. Step 4: localization is exact; the pigeonhole bound I^{r(N-1)+1}x=0 is correct; r=0 is handled separately. Step 5: g_S is in I, so L_{g_S}=0, and the localization/restriction exact adjunction via def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction gives Hom(L,U N)=0. Step 6: the column filtration is by subcomplexes, the quotients are U(K_{g_S})[-q] with the correct shift sign, and a finite descending induction uses the ses-triangle lemma and Hom-exactness with W=L[-m]. Step 7: composition with ε_K is injective (by (ii)) and surjective (by the rotated triangle and Step 6 with m=1); it is natural, the inclusion is the left adjoint and F the right adjoint. Step 8: for M[0] the total complex is literally C⊗M, and H∘Q≅H. Edge cases checked: r=0, the zero ring, a unit generator (RΓ_Z=0), a nilpotent generator (RΓ_Z=id), k[x] with M=A (H^1=k[x,x^{-1}]/k[x]), repeated generators, unbounded K. I grepped the DAG for 0A6R, extended Čech and torsion right adjoints and found no duplicate; the citers cech-bound and noetherian-comparison use the item consistently. No SGA. No faults from points B-E.
